official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statements related to the Central Administrative Tribunal are correct ?
I. It is a statutory body.
II. Its members are drawn from administrative background only.
III. It is not bound by the procedure prescribed in the Code of Civil Procedure.
IV. Its jurisdiction covers the members of All-India services as well as Central services and Central Government posts.
V. It was set up in 1985.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
official_questions.core_fact: CAT: statutory body under the Administrative Tribunals Act 1985 (Art. 323A), set up 1 Nov 1985; judicial and administrative members; not bound by CPC, follows natural justice; covers AIS, Central services and Central posts.

statements.t: The CAT is a statutory body.
CAT members are drawn from administrative background only.
statements.fact: CAT members come from judicial and administrative streams.

statements.t: The CAT is not bound by the procedure in the Code of Civil Procedure.
statements.d: not bound by the procedure ... Code of Civil Procedure

statements.t: CAT jurisdiction covers All-India services, Central services and Central posts.
statements.d: All-India services as well as Central services

statements.t: The CAT was set up in 1985.

official_questions.rule: CAT: Art. 323A (42nd Amendment) -> 1985 Act; members judicial + administrative; appeals to HC division bench (L. Chandra Kumar 1997).

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the National Green Tribunal ?
I. It was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
II. NGT is bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
III. NGT has six places of sitting throughout the country.
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
official_questions.core_fact: NGT: set up 18 Oct 2010 under the NGT Act 2010; not bound by CPC, guided by natural justice; five places of sitting – New Delhi (principal), Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai; disposes appeals within 6 months.

statements.t: The NGT was set up under the NGT Act, 2010.
The NGT is bound by the procedure of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
statements.d: bound by the procedure ... Code of Civil Procedure
statements.fact: The NGT is not bound by the CPC; it follows natural justice (s.19).

statements.t: The NGT has six places of sitting.
statements.fact: The NGT has five places of sitting.

official_questions.rule: NGT: 2010 Act, Art. 21 basis, 5 zones, not CPC-bound, appeals to SC within 90 days.

official_questions.stem:
With reference to the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements :
I. It was set up under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
II. Ministry of Welfare has notified five religious communities under “Minority” status, to date.
III. It can make recommendations for the effective implementation of safeguards for the protection of minorities by Central or State Governments.
Which of the above statements are correct ?
official_questions.core_fact: NCM: statutory under the NCM Act 1992; six notified minorities – Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis (1993) and Jains (2014) – notified by the Central Government (Ministry of Minority Affairs); recommends safeguards.

statements.t: The NCM was set up under the NCM Act, 1992.
The Ministry of Welfare has notified five religious communities as minorities to date.
statements.fact: Six communities are notified (Jains added 2014), by the Ministry of Minority Affairs.

statements.t: The NCM can recommend effective implementation of safeguards for minorities by governments.
statements.d: recommendations for the effective implementation of safeguards

official_questions.rule: Minorities: 5 in 1993 + Jains 2014 = 6; NCM statutory (1992), NCSC/NCST constitutional.

official_questions.stem:
With reference to the Competition Commission of India, consider the following statements :
I. It is a statutory body established under Competition Act, 2002 as amended by the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2007.
II. It consists of a chairperson and five members appointed by the Central Government.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
official_questions.core_fact: CCI: statutory body under the Competition Act 2002 (amended 2007), constituted 2003/operational 2009; chairperson and not less than 2 and not more than 6 members appointed by the Central Government (downsized to 1+3 in 2018).

statements.t: The CCI is a statutory body under the Competition Act, 2002 as amended in 2007.
The CCI consists of a chairperson and five members appointed by the Central Government.
statements.fact: The Act allows a chairperson and 2-6 members (1+6 originally, 1+3 after 2018) – not 'five'.

official_questions.rule: CCI: 2002 Act, 1+6 max (now 1+3 working); appeals to NCLAT (since 2017).

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are incorrect regarding the Law Commission of India ?
I. It is a non-constitutional quasi judicial body.
II. One of its functions is to communicate its opinion to the President on subjects relating to legal administration.
III. Its reports are not submitted to the Parliament.
IV. It has no suo motu decision power to undertake research by itself.
Select the answer using the codes given below :
official_questions.core_fact: The Law Commission is a non-constitutional, non-statutory executive body (set up by GoI order, 1955 onward), purely advisory; it advises the Government (Ministry of Law) on law reform, its reports are placed before Parliament, and it can take up subjects suo motu.

statements.t: The Law Commission is a non-constitutional quasi-judicial body.
statements.fact: It is advisory, not quasi-judicial.

statements.t: The Law Commission communicates its opinion to the President on legal administration.
statements.fact: It communicates its views to the Government (Ministry of Law), not the President.

statements.t: Law Commission reports are not submitted to Parliament.
statements.fact: Its reports are laid before Parliament.

statements.t: The Law Commission has no suo motu power to undertake research.
statements.fact: It can take up research suo motu.

official_questions.rule: Law Commission: executive, non-statutory, 3-year term; 22nd (Ritu Raj Awasthi), 23rd constituted 2024; first post-independence 1955 (M.C. Setalvad).
